findings.assumptions: The assessment introduces no mathematical assumption. The two accepted results it rests on are assumption-free beyond ZFC (acceptance-000001) and conditional on the named assumption RL(H) carried inside the statement of Corollary O' (acceptance-000002); the assessment's what_changed states the conditionality explicitly. The first next hypothesis asserts Problem 1.5 as a hypothesis with a failure signal, not as a fact; the second is scoped to the admissible class at leading order, which by the proof file's own axiomatisation (Section 4, item 1) includes the pairwise sign-model limit, so a failure of RL(H) counts as a mechanism outside the class. The supplied earlier assessments and acceptances were used for continuity and cross-checked against the delivered artifacts, not taken as authority. considered_failure_ids is empty, consistent with failure_signal_fired=false in both delivered journal moves.

openness.coverage: As reported in the delivered problem, novelty and strategy studies, all dated 2026-10-21: nine common-store searches, one per formulation (the exact root statement; the 1-subdivision of every graph, Problem 1.5; the 1-subdivision of the reported counterexample; a girth threshold; incidence graphs of linear hypergraphs; the Heawood graph; forcing for girth-six graphs; biregular girth-six graphs; Conjecture 4.1 of Im-Li-Liu), binding 25 captures: eleven arXiv API queries (mostly complete, up to 50 results), seven OpenAlex work searches (top 20 by relevance or complete when fewer), one complete OpenAlex citing-works query for Fox-Wei 2017, six earlier arXiv captures; Crossref 'Sidorenko conjecture girth' and '... subdivision' (top 20 each, relevance-ranked); zbMATH Open 'Sidorenko & girth' (5, complete), 'Sidorenko & subdivision' (6, complete), 'ti:Sidorenko' (51, complete); MathOverflow 'Sidorenko' (7) and 'Sidorenko girth' (0); strategy-study queries: arXiv regular/pendant/biregular (4 of 4, complete), arXiv barrier query (7 of 7, complete), Crossref subdivision-reduction (top 20 of 914,848) and barrier (top 20 of 287,470), zbMATH 'Sidorenko & tree' (21, complete) and 'Sidorenko & squares' (5, complete). Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 on every attempt and is an unavailable source. Seventeen full readings are reported in the common store. Delivered and read in full here: Conlon-Kim-Lee-Lee 2018 (Problem 1.5 stated open), Kim-Lee-Lee 2016, Coregliano-Razborov 2021, and [161], whose pattern has 4-cycles and so does not settle the girth-six statement. The search records with captured_at and coverage, the reading records and the cited common-store openness record 711410e0... are referenced by digest only and are not delivered.
openness.reason: The delivered studies describe a plausibly thorough search and report a prior common-store 'supported_open' finding for the root statement and its eight neighbours, but the bound literature_search records and the complete fulltext reading records are not among the delivered evidence, so they cannot be verified here and access must not be invented; Semantic Scholar was unavailable for every query; the full text of Fox-Wei 2017 was not read (its described content, a local theorem, could not settle the statement). These integrity and availability gaps permit only 'unresolved'. The four delivered full texts contain no result settling the root statement, consistent with but not establishing 'supported_open'. This does not block approval: the subject is a strategy reassessment that asserts no openness and seeks no root closure (native.subject carries no acceptance_ids), and every obligation remains open. The objective's openness milestone and any root closure remain pending until a review bound to the actual search and reading records is delivered.

findings.policy: proof_policy 'reviewed': the assessment cites only results that received observed independent reviews and acceptance under the reviewed standard, and I re-checked the obstruction argument against the delivered source text. requested_outcome 'decision' remains undelivered and the assessment does not pretend otherwise; remaining_obligation_ids lists all four obligations open and the route stays a hypothesis. Finite computation obligations: none claimed, none required. Resource policy: two moves in total across the objective (one per node) of at most 24, no runs of at most 24, one worker; within limits. Material new settling evidence for the root statement, Problem 1.5, or the premise outside C_2 would require a new observed review bound to that evidence before any closure; this approval authorizes only the recorded reassessment.
findings.scope: The assessment is scoped to this bounded attempt on objective-000001 (root statement: Sidorenko's inequality for every finite bipartite graph of girth at least six and every graphon). It establishes nothing about the root statement and claims nothing about it; it retires the two admitted nodes after their milestones were met and leaves route-000001 in status 'hypothesis' with all obligations open. The retire decisions are strategic judgments ('a new research programme beyond this bounded attempt'); this review has no strategic-value prerequisite and assesses only that the scientific record cited is accurate and the obligation accounting is preserved, which it is. The second hypothesis is correctly limited to leading order and the admissible class; it does not claim the premise outside C_2 is true or false. strategy_order and plan_bindings are empty, consistent with both nodes retired; the ranking blob 1746c10d... confirms the next strategy in order would have been attack-the-negative-side, matching the assessment's remark that a construction outside the admissible class would be the next step.
findings.statement: The subject is a strategy reassessment (the third) of objective-000001, not a proof, reduction or closure. It records: (1) node-000001 (reduce-and-translate) retired, its milestone c2-reduces-to-problem-1-5 met by acceptance-000001; (2) node-000002 (prove-the-barrier-first) retired, its milestone sign-model-barrier met by acceptance-000002; (3) two next hypotheses, one on obligation-000002 (Problem 1.5 holds, to be tested on base graphs outside the known classes) and one on obligation-000003 (a violating girth-six pattern outside C_2 would need a mechanism outside the admissible class of the reported construction at leading order); (4) all four obligations remain open; (5) a what_changed narrative of move 1 of node-000002 and acceptance-000002. I checked each statement against the delivered evidence. acceptance-000002 and checkpoint-000002 (blobs d9a0bde2..., b86e3793..., 3a39eb04...), the journal move 8d9c02a2..., the problem digest c66f9683... (direction 'unreachable') and the proof file ac528fd0... are all delivered and say what the assessment says they say. I spot-checked the obstruction proof against the delivered full text of [161] (3530e151...): Lemma O(a) is correct (two faces sharing points i,k form the 4-cycle i-j-k-j'-i, so each eta_P occurs in at most one factor and E(1+c_0 a eta_P)=1), Lemma O(b) gives 1+ab on a 4-cycle, and Corollary O' follows the coordinate regrouping of [161] Lemma 3.2 and the bipartite identity of Proposition 3.5; the transpose paragraph writes Y_i-X_j where X_j-Y_i is produced, harmless since RL(H) is assumed in both orientations and Lemma O holds for all signs. The what_changed correctly carries the conditionality on RL(H) and the leading-order restriction; the shorter retire reason for node-000002 ('excludes the one published refutation mechanism ... at leading order') omits the RL(H) conditionality, which is a presentational imprecision only, since the accepted checkpoint and what_changed state it. The pattern of [161] has every point pair in exactly two faces (Proposition 2.1 of the delivered text), so it has 4-cycles and does not bear on the root statement. The remaining_obligation_ids are correct: a reduction and a method-relative obstruction change no obligation status, and the root obligation, both premises and the bridge of route-000001 stay open.
